quirks: Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties; pre-1811 records are filed under the parent counties.
Probate records (wills, administrations) are held by the county Register of Wills, available from 1811 - a primary parentage source naming heirs.
Roman Catholic parishes fell under the Diocese of Philadelphia until the Diocese of Scranton was erected in 1868; sacramental registers are held at the parish/diocese, not the county.
Pennsylvania statewide civil birth/death registration did not begin until 1906; a 1908 death has a state certificate, but pre-1906 events rely on church, cemetery, and probate records.
Some naturalization and church films for the anthracite coal region are browse-only image groups (volume_search shows ~0% record-searchable) - browse image-by-image.

entry.rationale: The 1880 census is the first to include dedicated columns for the birthplace of each person's father and mother — the only census in the research window to do so systematically. Patrick Flynn (~age 35) would appear as head of his own household; that entry alone would report Thomas Flynn's birthplace as Patrick recalled it (corroborating paternity) and give the first direct clue to the mother's birthplace and identity. Thomas Flynn (~age 60s-70s) may also still be enumerable. Both Patrick and Thomas should be searched in Schuylkill County. This is the highest-value next step given known evidence gaps.

Thomas Flynn's 1870 household would name his wife by given name — the essential first step toward identifying the mother. The 1870 census does not state relationships but lists all household members; the wife would appear adjacent to Thomas with her given name and estimated birth year. These details are needed to search church and marriage records for her identity. Patrick (~age 25) may still be in the household or nearby in Schuylkill County. Search both Thomas and Patrick Flynn.

Per GPS planning standards, a parentage question requires a dedicated item for the candidate parents' marriage to each other. Thomas Flynn's marriage to Patrick's mother (estimated ~1835-1848, before Patrick's birth ~1845 in Ireland) would name the mother directly and establish the legal union. FamilySearch holds two indexed collections covering this period: 'Pennsylvania, Civil Marriages, 1677-1950' (col. 1571957) and 'Pennsylvania, Compiled Marriages, 1700-1900' (col. 1502909). Both should be searched with variant spellings — Flynn, Flyn, Flinn, Flin. Marriage may have taken place in Ireland before emigration, so a negative result here does not eliminate the hypothesis; it would redirect to Irish records.

Per loc_001 quirk: Schuylkill County Catholic parishes fell under the Diocese of Philadelphia until 1868, then the Diocese of Scranton. Sacramental registers are held at the parish/diocese level. FamilySearch volume 007936751 (Church Records 1842-1895, 0% record-searchable, browse-only) contains baptismal registers for local parishes. A baptismal entry for Patrick (~1845) or any Flynn sibling is direct parentage evidence, naming both father and mother. Volume must be browsed image-by-image. The 1860 census states Patrick was born in Ireland, so his own baptism may be absent — but younger siblings born in Pennsylvania after the family emigrated could appear here, and each sibling entry still names the same parents.

Patrick Flynn's own marriage record (likely 1860s-1880s given birth ~1845) may state his age, birthplace, and parents' names. FamilySearch volume 007936753 covers Schuylkill County marriage records 1870-1910 (0% indexed, browse-only). Also search the indexed collection 'Pennsylvania, County Marriages, 1885-1950' (col. 1921317) in case Patrick married after 1885. A witness or sponsor at Patrick's marriage who is also a neighbor from the 1850 household would extend the FAN evidence. Date window set to Patrick's plausible marriage years (age ~20-40 = 1865-1885, extended to 1910 for coverage).

In Pennsylvania, a married man conveying real property required his wife's signature as co-grantor (to bar her dower right). FamilySearch volume 007936752 (Deed Records 1815-1900, 22% indexed) could yield deeds where Thomas Flynn and wife jointly conveyed property — naming the wife (Patrick's mother) and confirming her identity. Search grantor and grantee indexes for Thomas Flynn and variant spellings. Date window set to Thomas's plausible land-ownership years from Patrick's birth (~1845) through Thomas's estimated death (~1900); window bounds derive from Thomas's likely lifespan, not Patrick's.

pli_006 searched the FamilySearch indexed probate records for Schuylkill County (1870-1900) and returned negative. However, FamilySearch volume 007936749 (Probate Records 1851-1930, 0% record-searchable, browse-only) is a distinct unindexed image group not covered by that indexed search. This volume must be browsed image-by-image for Thomas Flynn's will, administration, or estate inventory — any of which would name his heirs (including Patrick if he is a son) and possibly a surviving spouse.
